cockpit_overview.title: YOU ARE LOOKING AT A RECONSTRUCTED ENGINE COCKPIT
cockpit_overview.body:
Pandemic Studios shipped LOTR: Conquest in 2009 on a custom engine called Magellan. Months later EA shot the studio in the head mid-project and we got handed a corpse. This program is what happens when you spend years pulling the wreckage out of the river, reading hex dumps until your eyes bleed, and rewiring every gauge by hand off a stolen Havok 5.5 SDK that nobody documented because the people who would have documented it got fucking fired.

THE COCKPIT IS THE TOOL. Do not try to simplify it. Every knob exists because some Pandemic system needs to come back. Click the (?) icons next to section headers when you do not know what something does. The HOW TO USE button up top (red) re-opens this card any time. Help menu has 'Reset ALL Tips' to re-fire every popup.

HOW TO USE THIS FUCKING THING. The controls that actually do work:

FILE menu, Open Level. Pick a PAK file from RE/Levels or RE/mods/Levels. The cockpit lights up. Do not open two at once, the state thrashes and you lose unsaved edits.

TOOLS menu, Crowd Mesh Builder. Bake hero+weapon merges into crowd archetypes. EA killed the runtime weapon-attach code before shipping it, so we weld weapons into mesh slot[0] at build time. This panel is where you build new ones.

TOOLS, Crowd Mesh Builder, Move Triangles section (collapsing header at the bottom). For after you baked and the bow is 3cm too low. Click triangles in the embedded viewer, drag Delta XYZ, Apply, Save. Do not burn another five-minute re-bake.

TOOLS, Mesh Surgery. When a CRD has a sword welded in and you want it OUT. Picks verts by UV box or bone weight, queues a strip that runs at Save time.

TOOLS, Adjust Baked Weapon. Same job as Move Triangles but selects verts by bone weight. Useful for shipped CRDs where you do not know what the weapon triangles look like.

FILE, Save Level. Runs level_patcher.py plus lotrc_rs -c. Repacks the PAK with every edit you made this session. Takes minutes. Do NOT close the terminal window that pops up. If it errors out you LOSE the unsaved edits.

RIDE OR FUCKING DIE, KING. EAT IT.

viewport.title: THE MAIN VIEWPORT. WHERE THE WHOLE GODDAMN LEVEL ACTUALLY LIVES
viewport.body:
This is what Pandemic's level designers stared at when they built Helm's Deep, Minas Tirith, the Black Gates. We rebuilt the renderer from disassembly notes and the SDK shader registers and now it shows you the same scene the runtime engine shows the player. Same atlas pipeline, same lighting model, same skinning palette. The fucker WORKS.

HOW TO USE THE CAMERA:

- RIGHT-DRAG to look around (FPS-style).
- WASD to move while right-mouse is held.
- Q/E to drop/rise on world Y.
- SHIFT to sprint, CTRL to crawl.
- F to focus the camera on the selected entity. Camera flies to it like a goddamn pigeon homing on bread.
- LEFT-CLICK on anything to select it. Inspector populates.
- ALT+LEFT-DRAG inside the viewport orbits the camera around the selected entity. XSI style.

GIZMOS (when something is selected):

- W: translation gizmo. Drag any axis arrow to slide, drag a plane patch to slide in 2D.
- E: rotation gizmo. Drag a ring to rotate around that axis.
- R: scale gizmo. (Most level entities ignore scale; gameobj transforms are translation+rotation only, EA never wired animated scale on most types.)
- HOLD CTRL while dragging for snap (configurable in Gizmo Tools panel).

DANGERS THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Gizmo edits are LIVE, they write to the entity's WorldTransform field in Block1 immediately. No fucking undo. Save Level commits.
- Some entities have parent/child relationships (capture_zone owns its trigger volume, etc). Moving the parent moves the children. Inspect the hierarchy in Outliner if a move looked wrong.
- The viewport runs at the level's atmospheric tonemap. Dark levels (Black Gates) actually ARE that dark, that is not a bug. Pandemic shipped it that way. Use Model Viewer for individual mesh inspection with neutral lighting.

EAT IT.

browser.title: ASSET BROWSER. EVERY GODDAMN MODEL, ANIM, MAT, FX IN THE PAK
browser.body:
Pandemic's content team shipped thousands of assets per level before EA fed them all to the woodchipper. The runtime engine slurps them out of the PAK at load time and stuffs them in fixed-slot arrays. This panel shows you EVERY slot. Type by type, with hover preview and double-click drop-into-viewport.

HOW TO USE:

1. TAB BAR at the top: Models / Animations / Materials / Effects. Click to switch type.
2. SEARCH box per tab. Filters the list live. Most asset names follow Pandemic's prefix scheme (CH_, CRD_, WP_, FX_, GMR_, etc.), so 'elf' narrows the fuck down fast.
3. CLICK a row to select. Right side panel shows asset details (vert count, tri count, bone count, atlas refs, etc.).
4. DOUBLE-CLICK a Model to open it in Model Viewer.
5. DOUBLE-CLICK an Animation to start playing it on the current preview rig.
6. RIGHT-CLICK for context menu: Export (decompiles back to source-ish), Duplicate (in-place clone with new CRC), Find References (which entities/anim graphs use this).

WHAT EACH TAB CONTAINS:

- MODELS: every mesh in the PAK. Hero rigs (CH_), crowd archetypes (CRD_), weapons (WP_), props (PR_), level geo, foliage. Click and the model's atlas refs / bone count / tri count appear.
- ANIMATIONS: every animation clip. Pandemic compressed them with their own quat/translation codec because they had to make it fit on disc. Click to see frame count, sample rate, target skeleton.
- MATERIALS: every Mat1/Mat2/Mat3/Mat4 entry from Block1. tex0/tex1/tex2/tex3 refs, shader register state, blend mode.
- EFFECTS: particle systems, decals, screen-space FX. References to the FX_*.bin shader bundles.

SHIT THAT WILL BURN YOU:

- Duplicating an asset creates a new CRC in the PAK. If you don't reference it from somewhere, it ships as orphan data wasting space.
- Renaming an asset is NOT supported here. Use the binary RE pipeline if you need that. We didn't wire it because nobody asked yet.

EAT IT.

outliner.title: OUTLINER. THE LEVEL'S CURSED HIERARCHY TREE, RECONSTRUCTED FROM HEX
outliner.body:
Pandemic's editor (ZeroEdit) had a hierarchical outliner where every layer, every group, every entity nested under its parent. This panel reconstructs that view from the level's Block1 parent/child CRC references. Built it by reading hex dumps until the relationships made fucking sense.

HOW TO USE:

1. EXPAND/COLLAPSE tree nodes by clicking the arrow. Top level is templateLevel, then Layers, then entities within layers.
2. CLICK an entity to select. Highlighted in viewport. Inspector populates.
3. DOUBLE-CLICK to focus camera on it.
4. RIGHT-CLICK for context menu: Rename, Duplicate, Delete, Reparent.
5. DRAG and DROP an entity onto another to reparent. The cascade move recalculates child WorldTransforms relative to the new parent.
6. SEARCH bar filters the tree. Shows the matching nodes plus their parent chain so you can see WHERE in the hierarchy they live.

LAYER CONTROLS (per row, on the right):

- EYE icon: hide/show this layer in the viewport. Editor only, doesn't affect game runtime.
- LOCK icon: prevent selection/edits on this layer. Stops you fat-fingering the entire fucking layer when you meant to grab one child.
- ISOLATE button: hides every OTHER layer. Click again to un-isolate.
- ACTIVE radio: which layer new entities (from CREATE wizard) get placed into by default.

SHIT THAT EATS YOU:

- REPARENTING via drag changes the entity's parent_crc field in Block1. The runtime engine respects parent/child for transform cascade. If you drag a capture_zone child away from its capture_zone parent, the relationship breaks in-game and the cap zone goes dark.
- Deleting a layer from the tree does NOT delete its child entities. They orphan with no fucking parent. Either delete children first or use the Level panel's WIPE command which cascades.
- Some entities are children of HIDDEN system layers (the LightingLayer, the AudioLayer). They show up filtered unless you toggle 'Show System Layers' in the menu.

EAT IT.

gizmo_tools.title: GIZMO TOOLS. CONFIG FOR THE GODDAMN MANIPULATORS
gizmo_tools.body:
Controls for the W/E/R translate/rotate/scale gizmos in the viewport. Pandemic used XSI's manipulator style internally before the EA buzzsaw came through. The F4-XSI authoring shell mimics it here. This panel is where you set snap, axis space, pivot mode. Get it wrong and your translations drift like a drunk pigeon, broken-by-design and bleeding all over the world matrix.

HOW TO USE:

1. SPACE toggle: WORLD vs LOCAL. World gizmos align to world axes. Local aligns to the entity's own orientation. For rotating something into a particular world direction, use WORLD. For incremental yaw on an entity that's already tilted, LOCAL is less fucking confusing.
2. PIVOT toggle: CENTER vs INDIVIDUAL. When you select multiple entities, CENTER puts one gizmo at the group center (rotations spin all of them around that point). INDIVIDUAL puts a gizmo per entity (each rotates around its own pivot).
3. SNAP toggle: ON/OFF. When on, holding CTRL while dragging snaps to the increments below.
4. TRANSLATION SNAP: meters. Default 0.5m. Set 0.1 for fine, 1.0 for tile alignment.
5. ROTATION SNAP: degrees. Default 15. Set 5 for fine, 45/90 for level-block alignment.
6. SCALE SNAP: factor. Default 0.1.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- World/Local is per-tool and saved. If you switched to Local for a specific job and forgot, your next translation drags along bizarre angles. Check the toggle when something feels off.
- Snap doesn't apply unless CTRL is held DURING the drag. Toggling Snap on without holding CTRL still gives smooth motion. Pandemic's original was the same way, don't blame us.
- Most level entities ignore scale (gameobj WorldTransform is translation+rotation only). The R gizmo will animate but the engine won't render the scale. Pandemic never wired animated scale on gameobjs and we didn't bolt it on.

EAT IT.

the_forge.title: THE FORGE. ONE FUCKING PANEL THAT DOES THE WORK OF FOUR
the_forge.body:
Phase 9 of the XSI authoring shell. Pandemic's level designers worked in a single mega-panel that had outliner, layers, event graph, properties all in one fucking place. The Forge is that mega-panel reconstructed. No more tab-juggling between four panels to do one job.

WHAT'S IN HERE (tab bar at top):

- OUTLINER: hierarchical entity tree (same content as the standalone Outliner panel).
- LAYERS: the layer manager (hide/lock/isolate). Edits persist in editor_filter.ini so you don't lose your hides every session.
- EVENT GRAPH: the trigger wiring (same content as the standalone Event Graph panel).
- PROPERTIES: a per-entity field-level editor (same as Inspector but for the selected Forge entity).
- ANIMATION: anim graph view for the selected character.

HOW TO USE:

1. Pick a tab. The view mode swaps.
2. Workflow: select an entity in OUTLINER, switch to PROPERTIES to inspect/edit, switch to EVENT GRAPH to see its trigger wiring, switch to LAYERS to manage visibility groups. The selection persists across tabs.
3. F4 (default hotkey): toggles The Forge on/off. Same key XSI used. Memorize it or suffer.
4. Sub-panel split: drag the vertical splitter to give more room to the main view vs the side panel.

SHIT THAT WILL BITE YOU:

- The Forge owns the same global state as the standalone Outliner/Event Graph/Layers panels. Don't open both simultaneously, they'll fight over which one drew first and you'll get goddamn flicker.
- Properties tab edits go to the same FieldEdit queue as the Inspector. Save Level commits them.

EAT IT.

level_blocks.title: LEVEL BLOCKS. THE RAW BLOCK1 SHITSHOW LAID BARE
level_blocks.body:
Pandemic's level format stores every entity as a binary blob in Block1, indexed by GUID, with a typed schema per entity type. This panel is the structural view: every block, every offset, every byte count. The closest thing to a fucking debugger we have for level files.

WHAT IT SHOWS:

- BLOCK1 / BLOCK2 / BLOCK3 split: the level file's three sections (entities / strings / scripts).
- Per-block: byte size, entry count, schema if known.
- Per-entry: type name, GUID, byte offset, payload size.

HOW TO USE:

1. Click a block to expand its entry list.
2. Click an entry to see its raw bytes (hex view at the bottom).
3. Click the schema icon next to an entry to open the typed view in Asset Data Inspector (F6 hotkey panel).
4. STATS at the bottom: total entity count, total field count, total bytes per block. Useful when comparing level sizes (Helm's Deep is fucking huge, Coricelesti's DLC blueprint is tiny).

SHIT THAT EATS YOU:

- Asset Data Inspector edits go directly to the decompressed Block1 buffer. Save Level repacks. Bad edits crash the runtime at load time with no error, the engine just shits the bed and quits.
- Don't edit block headers, only entry payloads. The block headers are managed by the patcher.

EAT IT.

cinematic_setup.title: CINEMATIC SETUP. EDIT THE CUTSCENE CAMERA WITHOUT TOUCHING THE GODDAMN BINARY
cinematic_setup.body:
Pandemic's cinematics ran on scripted cameras: a spline path through 3D space, with rotation curves, FOV curves, and trigger events at specific times. This panel reconstructs and lets you edit those rigs without diving into the goddamn binary.

WHAT'S IN HERE:

- 3D SPLINE EDIT MODE (FABRIK): drag spline control handles in the viewport to reshape the camera path. FABRIK keeps the spline smooth while you yank one control point so you don't get sharp fucking kinks.
- CAMERA PICKER: which cinematic_camera entity to edit. Each level has multiple (intro, mid-mission, outro).
- TIME SLIDER: scrub through the cutscene. Camera position previews live.
- KEYFRAME PANEL: each spline control point has time / position / rotation / FOV. Add/remove/move keyframes from this list.
- TRIGGER EVENTS: at time T, fire event E. For dialog timing, music cues, gameplay handoff.

HOW TO USE:

1. CAMERA PICKER dropdown. Pick the cinematic_camera you want to edit.
2. Click ENTER 3D SPLINE EDIT to drag handles in the viewport directly. Click EXIT to leave the mode.
3. Drag the TIME SLIDER to scrub. Viewport shows what the camera sees at that moment.
4. Click ADD KEYFRAME to drop a new handle at the current time + camera position.
5. Drag a keyframe in the list to reorder by time. Pandemic's playback resolves keys by time, not by index.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Spline editor edits the camera path immediately. The cinematic_camera's spline_data field gets rewritten. Save Level commits.
- Trigger events fire ONCE per playback. If you want a repeating trigger, set the event entity's auto_reset flag.
- FOV is in DEGREES not radians. Pandemic's runtime expects degrees. If your cutscene looks like a fisheye, you typed 90 thinking it was radians and now Aragorn has a goddamn cone for a head.

EAT IT.

bezier_curves.title: BEZIER CURVE EDITOR. ANIM CURVES YANKED OUT OF THE FUCKING BINARY
bezier_curves.body:
Pandemic's animation pipeline stored translation/rotation/scale per bone per frame, with optional Bezier curve interpolation for smooth blends. This panel exposes those curves channel-by-channel. Maya-style, dragged out of the binary by hand because the engineers who would have documented the format got fired before they could write the wiki.

HOW TO USE:

1. CHANNEL TABS: Rotation / Translation / Scale. Pick which channel you're editing.
2. BONE PICKER: which bone's curves to show.
3. AXIS PICKER (per channel): X/Y/Z for translation/scale, quaternion components for rotation.
4. THE CURVE: time on X axis, value on Y. Drag handles to reshape. Drag a control point to move the key. Drag a tangent handle to adjust the curve's shape into/out of that key.
5. ADD KEY: click on the timeline at the desired time. A new keyframe drops there.
6. DELETE KEY: select the key, press Delete.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Rotation curves operate in quaternion space (qx, qy, qz, qw). Drawing a 'smooth' line in quaternion-component-space does NOT give you a smooth rotation, the math just doesn't fucking work that way. Pandemic's runtime slerps between keys, the curve here just shows you the keyed component value.
- Edits go to the loaded animation's in-memory curve data. To commit, you'd have to repack the .anim asset which the current pipeline doesn't fully support yet.
- Some shipped animations have curves baked-out (sampled at fixed rate, no Bezier). Those show as a stair-step in this editor. Editing them treats each step as a key.

EAT IT.

lua_animtable.title: LUA ANIMTABLE. WHICH CLIP PLAYS WHEN FOR EACH CHARACTER
lua_animtable.body:
Pandemic's anim system has two halves: the BINARY graph (state machine, runs in-engine, what the runtime actually reads) and the LUA-generated animTable (per-character config: 'when player is in DRAW_BOW state, play clip A_BOW_DRAW_01'). This panel edits the Lua side. The half that doesn't actually do shit at runtime but is the source of truth for what Pandemic INTENDED.

HOW TO USE:

1. CHARACTER picker. Which character/CRD's animTable to view.
2. ENTRIES: each row is one state-to-clip binding. State name, clip name, loop mode, blend time.
3. Click ADD ENTRY to bind a new state/clip pair.
4. EDIT in place: change the clip name, change the loop mode (Once / Loop / Hold), change blend in/out times.
5. APPLY writes the changes to the Lua source file in the dump dir.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- The Lua animTable is generated FROM the binary graph by Pandemic's source pipeline. Editing the Lua here doesn't regenerate the binary, and the binary is what the runtime actually reads. So your Lua edits look right but the game ignores them.
- Useful as a REFERENCE view (see what Pandemic INTENDED) more than as an authoring tool. For binary edits use the Animation Graph panel.
- Clip name typos silently fail at runtime. The state falls back to idle and nothing tells you.

EAT IT.

anim_state_machine.title: ANIMATION STATE MACHINE. THE BINARY GRAPH AND PANDEMIC'S CORPSE-LUA IN A BARE-KNUCKLE FACE-OFF
anim_state_machine.body:
Side-by-side comparison of the binary animation graph and the source-side Lua representation. For when you're trying to figure out whether what's in the PAK matches what Pandemic shipped in their internal Lua scripts. Drift between them is fucking common after manual edits.

WHAT IT SHOWS:

- BINARY column: states/transitions as they exist in the PAK.
- LUA column: same data as Pandemic's source Lua would have produced.
- DIFF column: where they disagree.

HOW TO USE:

1. CHARACTER picker (same one as Animation Graph).
2. ASM PARITY TOGGLES at the bottom: which checks to run (state count, transition count, clip references, blend times, etc.).
3. CLICK a row to highlight it in the binary graph view.
4. SHIPPED LEVELS are mostly already in parity (Pandemic was internally consistent before EA fucked them). Drift appears when you edit the binary in Animation Graph without regenerating the Lua.

SHIT TO WATCH:

- Parity drift is a 'leak' indicator: somebody edited binary without touching source. If you're shipping a level mod and rely on script behavior, regenerate Lua too.
- This panel is read-only on the data. Edit in Animation Graph (binary) or Lua AnimTable (Lua) panels.

EAT IT.

filter_selection.title: FILTER SELECTION + GRAPH STATE + MOTION MATCHING
filter_selection.body:
Three Pandemic systems jammed into one fucking panel because they all chain into the same runtime evaluator: which animation to pick next based on player input, current state, and motion-matching candidates.

FILTER SELECTION:

- Per-state, per-transition: a filter expression that decides whether this transition is valid right now. 'IsGrounded() AND HasWeapon() AND NOT IsStaggered()'.
- Edit the expression string. Syntax is Pandemic's mini-DSL.

GRAPH STATE:

- Live view of the runtime state vars: which state the player is in, what clip is playing, what frame.
- Useful when debugging WHY a transition isn't firing.

MOTION MATCHING:

- Pandemic's locomotion blend system: pick the best clip from a pool based on the player's velocity, direction, and pose.
- This panel shows the candidate clips and their match scores in real time.

HOW TO USE:

1. Bind a character to the live preview (use Animation Graph's character picker).
2. Drive the player around in-viewport (if the preview supports it; some levels have spawn points).
3. Watch the panels update: see which filters pass, which transitions fire, which motion-match clip wins.
4. Tune filter expressions / motion-match weights in the side panel. Edits queue for Save Level.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Filter expressions are a DSL, not Lua. Typos silently evaluate to false. Use the syntax-check button before saving or you'll be staring at a character that just stands the fuck there in-game.
- Motion matching is computationally expensive. Adding too many candidate clips per state burns CPU at runtime. Pandemic shipped with ~20 per state typical.

EAT IT.

timeline.title: TIMELINE. SCRUB, EDIT, OR OBLITERATE EVERY GODDAMN FRAME
timeline.body:
Pandemic's animator panel: the time bar at the bottom, play/pause/scrub, frame markers, event flags, bone-channel rows showing where keys exist. The classic DCC timeline that every Maya/XSI user has burned into their fucking retinas. Reconstructed from the cursed binary because Pandemic's source-side animator tools went into the dirt with the studio.

HOW TO USE:

1. PLAY / PAUSE / STEP buttons at the left.
2. TIME SLIDER: drag to scrub. Frame indicator shows current frame.
3. PLAYBACK RATE: 0.5x / 1x / 2x / 4x. Useful for studying fast attack anims at quarter speed.
4. LOOP toggle: when scrub reaches end, jump to start.
5. CHANNEL ROWS: each visible bone gets a row. Dots = keyframes. Click a dot to select the key. Drag to move in time.
6. EVENT FLAGS: vertical lines on the timeline mark event triggers (footstep, hitbox-on, hitbox-off, etc.). Click to inspect/edit.
7. POSE SNAPSHOT button: capture current bone state to a clipboard. Paste at a different time to copy the pose.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Dragging keys in time changes the animation timing. Edits queue for Save Level. The .anim asset gets rewritten.
- Event flags fire ONCE during playback. The runtime expects them at specific frames. Move a footstep event and the audio cue desyncs and the player hears the boot land before the foot does.
- Loop toggle is editor-only. The runtime loop behavior is controlled by the anim graph state's loop_mode, not by this fucking toggle.

EAT IT.

overlay.title: OVERLAY. THE GODDAMN HUD BLEEDING OVER THE VIEWPORT
overlay.body:
Top-left HUD overlay that the editor draws over the 3D viewport: FPS counter, camera position readout, selected entity name, gizmo mode indicator, current level name. Same idea as Unreal's stat overlay, except this one doesn't fucking lie about frame times.

WHAT'S IN HERE:

- FPS (top corner): renderer frame rate. Drops below 30 means something's wrong.
- FRAME TIME (ms): more useful than FPS for spotting hitches.
- CAMERA POS: x/y/z world coords. Useful for placing entities at known coordinates.
- CAMERA ROT: yaw/pitch (degrees).
- SELECTED: name of the currently-selected entity.
- GIZMO MODE: W (translate) / E (rotate) / R (scale).
- LEVEL: name of the loaded level.

HOW TO USE:

1. Open via View menu. The overlay is non-blocking, click-through.
2. Drag the overlay window to reposition. The location persists in imgui.ini.
3. Hide what you don't need: right-click the overlay for a checkbox list of which stats to display.
4. The overlay does NOT block clicks on the viewport beneath it, so you can have it floating in the middle of your scene without losing selection.

DANGER:

- The overlay updates every frame. Heavy stats (per-frame entity count, etc.) cost CPU. Hide the ones you don't watch or you're paying for shit you never read.

EAT IT.

level_inspector.title: LEVEL INSPECTOR. THE WORLD TRANSFORM EDITOR FOR ANY ENTITY
level_inspector.body:
F4 opens this. Field-level transform inspector: pure position/rotation matrix view of the selected entity, with editable XYZ position, quaternion or euler rotation, optional scale. Same data the gizmo edits, but exposed as numeric fields for when you need precise fucking placement, not eyeball-it-and-drag.

HOW TO USE:

1. Select an entity in the viewport or Outliner. The inspector populates.
2. IDENTITY section: shows GUID, type, name.
3. POSITION section: X / Y / Z meters in world space. Type directly for precise placement.
4. ROTATION section: yaw / pitch / roll in degrees. Or click 'Quat' to edit as quaternion components.
5. SCALE section: per-axis scale (most entities ignore this).
6. PASTE TRANSFORM button: paste a transform from clipboard (set by the COPY TRANSFORM button on another entity).
7. SAVE PAK button: queues the level for save. Same as File menu Save Level.

SAVE SUMMARY appears at the bottom: how many pending entities / field edits / deleted GUIDs / collision meshes will go to the next save. Hover for the breakdown tooltip.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- World-space numeric edit. If you want to move RELATIVE to the entity's current pose, use the viewport gizmo with Local space. Typing relative deltas here means doing the math in your head and that's how you end up with a capture zone in the goddamn skybox.
- Quaternion edits aren't normalized for you. Type 0/0/0/0 and the rotation goes haywire. Stick to euler unless you know what you're doing.
- 'Save Summary' counts queued changes. If the count is non-zero and you forgot to Save Level, those edits live ONLY in this session and die when you close Vespucci.

EAT IT.

editor_object.title: EDITOR OBJECT. PANDEMIC'S 'WHAT TO SHOW IN VIEWPORT' FILTER
editor_object.body:
F5 opens this. Pandemic's editor had per-object visibility filters: 'show only objects in category X / within distance Y from camera / labeled with Z'. This panel reconstructs and persists the filter state in editor_filter.ini so you don't have to re-set your hides every fucking session.

HOW TO USE:

1. CATEGORY mask: which entity categories to render in the editor (spawn points, lights, cameras, AI, capture zones, trigger volumes, sound emitters, etc.). Checkboxes per category.
2. DISTANCE filter: hide objects past N meters from the camera. Default off. Set to e.g. 50 to declutter while working in a small area.
3. LABEL DISTANCE: editor draws floating name labels above entities. This is the max distance at which labels are visible.
4. SEARCH bar: filters by name. Only entities matching the substring are drawn.
5. SAVE PAK at the bottom commits any pending edits.

SHIT TO REMEMBER:

- These filters are EDITOR-ONLY. They don't affect the game runtime. So if your spawn point is visible in-game but not here, that's filtering not deletion.
- Filter state persists across sessions in editor_filter.ini next to the exe. Delete the goddamn ini if you've nuked your filters and want defaults back.
- Aggressive filters can hide entities you forgot you turned off. If 'I can't find my spawn point' is happening, check the category mask first before you start panicking.

EAT IT.

asset_data_inspector.title: F6. RAW BINARY HEX EDITOR FOR ANY BLOCK1 STRUCT
asset_data_inspector.body:
The deepest fucking panel in the cockpit. Pandemic's level format stores entities and assets as typed C structs in Block1. This panel reads the schema, displays every field with its type and current value, and lets you edit in place. It's a hex editor with names. Lit up by year-long binary archaeology.

WHAT'S IN HERE:

- Categories of structs: Mat1 (92 bytes, 23 fields), Mat2, Mat3, Mat4, BufferInfo, VBuffInfo, IBuffInfo, ShapeInfo, HkShapeInfo, ModelInfo, AssetHandle.
- Per-struct: field name, type (u32/f32/CRC/vec3/mat4/etc.), current value, edit widget.
- HEX/DECIMAL/FLOAT toggle: switch how integer fields display.
- RAW HEX DUMP: collapsing section showing the raw bytes side-by-side with ASCII.

HOW TO USE:

1. CATEGORY picker. Pick the struct type you want to inspect.
2. INDEX picker. Pick which entry in that category (Mat1 has hundreds in a typical level).
3. EDIT FIELDS in the typed form. Changes go to the decompressed Block1 buffer immediately.
4. SAVE PAK at the bottom queues the changes for save.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU AND BURY THE BODY:

- THIS IS THE NUCLEAR OPTION. Edits write raw bytes to the binary blob. Bad struct field values crash the runtime at load time with no error message, the engine just shits the bed and quits.
- Always know what each field DOES before editing. The probes we ran for mat.tex2 / mat.key / mat.flags came through this panel and proved most fields don't fucking matter for crowds (see project_crowd_shader_limits.md).
- HkShapeInfo edits MUST go through the ShapeInfo chain or Havok crashes (see project_collision_fix memory).
- SAVE PAK overwrites the original PAK. Have a backup of your Levels dir or you're gonna cry.

EAT IT.

crowd_editor.title: 3DCROWD EDITOR. EDIT THE 3DCROWD HEADER BLOCK DIRECTLY
crowd_editor.body:
The 3dCrowd block in Block1 stores every crowd archetype + every instance in the level. This panel exposes the raw structure: archetype name, mesh ref, animation ref, instance list, per-instance position/rotation/LOD. Brutal direct access, nothing held back.

WHAT'S IN HERE (compared to Crowd Inspector / Crowd Generator):

- Crowd INSPECTOR shows individual instances and lets you edit transform/animation per-instance.
- Crowd GENERATOR bulk-spawns N instances of an archetype.
- Crowd EDITOR is the structural view: every archetype's raw fields, the engine-side hookups (which Lua callback fires at spawn, which event fires at death, etc.).

HOW TO USE:

1. ARCHETYPE picker. Top-level list of every 3dCrowd item in the level.
2. FIELDS panel: every header field of the archetype. Mesh ref, anim ref, LOD distance, max instance count, spawn callback, death callback, etc.
3. INSTANCE LIST: every spawned instance with its position/rotation/LOD/runtime state.
4. EDIT fields in place. Save Level commits.
5. ADD ARCHETYPE: create a NEW 3dCrowd entry for a freshly-baked CRD. Lets you wire the just-baked mesh into the level so it actually spawns instead of sitting in the PAK as dead fucking weight.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- The crowd subsystem is the proxy DLL's heaviest hookup area. See project_crowd_dll_findings.md for what the DLL already intercepts.
- The in-game crowd shader hardcodes to tex0 ignoring material data; see project_crowd_shader_limits.md. So editing mat.tex1/tex2 here does fuck-all in-game.
- Editing instance counts past Pandemic's internal limits (~5000) crashes the engine. Stay under 2000 per archetype.

EAT IT.

inspector_clip.title: INSPECTOR CLIP SECTION. WHICH ANIMATION IS CURRENTLY LOADED
inspector_clip.body:
The dumbest fucking question this panel answers, but the one you ask first when something looks haunted: which goddamn clip is even loaded. Top of the Inspector Info tab. Shows the model name + clip name driving the preview. Read-only here, edit via the Animation Graph panel.

USE: at a glance, see WHICH anim clip the preview is running. If the playback looks wrong, this is the first place to check what's actually loaded vs what you intended. Mismatched clip is the most common cause of 'why is my preview broken' bullshit, and Pandemic shipped half their state machines with subtle naming collisions before the EA buzzsaw came through, so the wrong clip slipping in is born-broken behavior the engine never bothered to warn about.

EAT IT.

inspector_playback.title: PLAYBACK CONTROLS. PLAY/PAUSE/SCRUB FOR THE PREVIEW
inspector_playback.body:
The same goddamn transport every DCC has shipped since the Stone Age, except Pandemic's version is the one that survived after the studio went into the dirt. Play, pause, step forward/back, scrub bar, loop toggle. Same as Timeline panel but always-visible without the channel rows cluttering your eyes.

HOW TO USE:

1. PLAY button toggles play/pause.
2. STEP buttons advance/rewind one frame.
3. SCRUB bar drag for arbitrary time.
4. LOOP makes the clip restart from frame 0 after the end.

DANGER: editor-only loop, doesn't change the .anim asset's loop mode (that's in the anim graph state). So your in-game clip might not loop even if this toggle is on, and the runtime won't say a goddamn word about it. Born broken, ships broken.

EAT IT.

inspector_timing.title: TIMING. PLAYBACK RATE AND TIME SCALE FOR THE PREVIEW
inspector_timing.body:
The fucking dial that slows time down so you can see what Pandemic's animators actually shipped before the EA murder weekend cut their pipeline tools off at the knees. Playback rate multiplier for the preview. 1.0 = real-time, 0.5 = half-speed, 2.0 = double, etc. Negative goes backward, which lets you reverse-engineer what attack frame actually does the damage when the goddamn hit registration looks wrong.

USE: for studying attack hit-frames at quarter speed, set 0.25x and step through. For seeing where loops start/end, 4x. For fucking with the boss-fight choreography until it reads right, scrub manually like a tired bastard.

EDITOR-ONLY. The runtime ignores this entirely. Each anim graph state has its own playback_rate field, and the binary doesn't give a single fuck about what the editor shows.

EAT IT.

inspector_timewarp.title: TIME WARP. NON-LINEAR PLAYBACK CURVE
inspector_timewarp.body:
The goddamn secret sauce Pandemic used to make their attack anims hit like a hydrogen bomb strapped to a grenade launcher. Instead of linear playback (frame F at time T), the curve maps time to a non-linear sample point. Used for impact emphasis: slow into hit, fast out. The thing that makes a sword swing READ HEAVY instead of looking like a limp-wristed fucking noodle.

WHAT YOU SEE: a curve editor (time-in vs time-out). Drag the curve handles to reshape, watch the preview snap to the new timing.

DANGER: editing the time-warp curve writes to the anim graph state's timewarp_curve field. Save Level commits. Bad curves make the anim play backwards or stutter like a drunk pigeon, and the runtime won't warn you because Pandemic's error-handling died on the EA murder weekend.

EAT IT.

inspector_root_motion.title: ROOT MOTION. WHAT THE ROOT BONE DRIVES
inspector_root_motion.body:
The cursed switch that decides whether the anim moves the character or the character moves itself. Pandemic's anim system supports root motion: the animation can drive the entity's world position (running anim moves the character forward) or NOT (idle anim doesn't move the character or you'd have idle Aragorn moonwalking across Helm's Deep like a brainrotted fucker).

FIELDS:

- ENABLED toggle: yes/no for this clip.
- AXIS mask: which world axes get driven (XYZ, just XZ for horizontal-only locomotion, etc.).
- ROTATION root motion: yes/no for the root bone driving entity rotation.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU SIDEWAYS:

- Mid-animation root motion changes can teleport the character to fucking Mordor. Test in-game or you'll be chasing a haunted bug for a whole afternoon.
- Editing here writes to the clip's metadata. Save Level commits, and the runtime swallows the change without complaint, which means broken-by-design root motion behavior ships if you don't verify.

EAT IT.

inspector_compression.title: COMPRESSION SETTINGS. HOW THE CLIP IS PACKED IN THE PAK
inspector_compression.body:
The duct-taped-to-reality codec Pandemic shipped because they had to fit hundreds of fucking clips on a 2009 DVD before the EA buzzsaw came through and ate the entire pipeline. Per-bone, per-channel quantization with no fucking documentation because the engineers who would have written the wiki got fired before they could. This section shows the codec used and lets you adjust per-channel quantization.

FIELDS:

- CODEC: which compression algorithm (raw, quantized, curve-fitted).
- TRANS QUANT: translation channel quantization bits per axis.
- ROT QUANT: rotation channel quantization bits per quaternion component.
- SCALE QUANT: scale channel.

SHIT TO REMEMBER OR PAY FOR LATER:

- LOWER quantization saves PAK size but introduces visible animation jitter. Drop too far and your character jerks like they have a goddamn seizure.
- DEFAULT settings match what Pandemic shipped before the layoffs hit. Only change for size-critical scenarios.
- Editing requires re-encoding the clip, which the current pipeline supports for raw codec only. Quantized re-encode is in the Pandemic-shaped void in the documentation, still waiting on a brave bastard to figure it out.

EAT IT.

inspector_tools.title: INSPECTOR TOOLS. UTILITY BUTTONS FOR THE LOADED CLIP
inspector_tools.body:
The goddamn Swiss Army shitshow of one-shot buttons that operate on the currently-loaded animation clip. The 'do something useful with this fucking thing or set it on fire' cabinet.

BUTTONS:

- RESET TO BIND POSE: snaps the preview to T-pose, useful for inspecting the mesh without anim interfering.
- BAKE TIMEWARP: applies the time-warp curve and saves a new clip with linear playback.
- EXPORT TO FBX: dumps the clip + skeleton as FBX for external editing (Maya, Blender). For when you want to drag the corpse out of the byte salad and into a real DCC.
- IMPORT FROM FBX: replaces the clip with FBX content. WARNING: skeleton must match exactly, no fucking exceptions.
- VALIDATE: checks the clip for common errors (zero-length channels, NaN values, orphan bone refs).

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU SIDEWAYS:

- BAKE TIMEWARP destroys the original curve. Backup the clip first or you can't go back, the original is gone, eat it.
- IMPORT FROM FBX requires the FBX skeleton to have matching bone names AND hierarchy. Mismatches silently load garbage and you'll see a character convulsing in the viewport like a brainrotted muppet. Born broken, ships broken.

EAT IT.

inspector_transform.title: TRANSFORM. THE PREVIEW RIG'S WORLD MATRIX
inspector_transform.body:
The exact same goddamn XYZ + rotation + scale fields as F4 Level Inspector, except scoped to the preview rig only. Where the rig is parked in the viewport for editing, nothing more, nothing less.

EDITOR-ONLY. Doesn't affect the in-game entity's transform one single fucking bit. For that, use F4 Level Inspector on the actual gameobj entity, not this preview rig. Confusing the two is how you spend an afternoon wondering why your edits don't ship.

EAT IT.

inspector_curves.title: CURVES. BEZIER VIEW FOR THE SELECTED BONE
inspector_curves.body:
Same content as the Bezier Curve Editor panel but in-line. Shows the rotation/translation/scale curves for the currently-selected bone.

USE: quick curve inspection without opening the full fucking Bezier panel.

DANGER: edits here write to the clip's curve data, same as the Bezier panel. Save Level commits.

EAT IT.

inspector_export.title: EXPORT. DUMP THE CURRENT CLIP TO DISK
inspector_export.body:
Export the currently-loaded clip to a sidecar format for backup or external editing.

FORMATS: FBX (full skeleton + curves), JSON (text dump of every key), CSV (one row per frame per channel).

USE: scripted batch jobs, external curve editing in a real DCC (Maya), debugging by diffing two clips side-by-side when you need to know why one looks fucked.

EAT IT.

inspector_ik.title: IK. INVERSE KINEMATICS RIG CONFIG
inspector_ik.body:
Pandemic's cursed IK system, reconstructed from the binary because the source-side rigging tools went into the dirt with the studio. Per-character, define IK chains (foot to hip, hand to shoulder) that drive bone rotations to hit a world target. The fucking thing that keeps Aragorn's feet on the ground instead of clipping through the goddamn terrain when he stands on a slope. Without IK he'd skate around like a brainrotted muppet on ice.

FIELDS:

- CHAINS list: each chain's name, bones involved, target entity ref, blend weight.
- POLE VECTOR per chain: which way the elbow/knee bends.
- WEIGHT: 0 = pure FK, 1 = pure IK, 0.5 = blend.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU SIDEWAYS:

- IK runs at runtime per frame. Heavy chains cost CPU. Stack too many and your framerate eats shit.
- Pole vector typos make limbs bend backward. Your hero's elbow points the wrong fucking way and the animation looks like a puppet show run by a drooling bastard.
- Edits write to the character's IK rig data. Save Level commits. The cursed Havok 5.5 SDK has its own opinion about constraint solving, and ours doesn't always match.

EAT IT.

inspector_physics.title: PHYSICS. HAVOK RAGDOLL HOOKUP
inspector_physics.body:
The Havok hellscape that Pandemic welded into the engine before the EA buzzsaw came through. Pandemic shipped on Havok 5.5, the cursed 2009 SDK nobody documented, and characters have ragdoll rigs (per-bone rigid bodies + constraints) that activate on death. The thing that makes orcs flop like dead fucking fish when you drop them. Without ragdoll they'd die in T-pose like brainrotted scarecrows.

FIELDS:

- RAGDOLL ASSET: which Havok ragdoll file to use.
- ACTIVATE ON: death / damage / scripted.
- MASS / FRICTION / RESTITUTION per body.

SHIT YOU NEED TO KNOW OR YOU WILL EAT IT:

- Havok ragdoll edits go through the binary Havok format. Only certain fields are editable from here without a Havok SDK round-trip into the byte salad.
- ALWAYS use Havok 5.5.0, never any Newer Havok version (see feedback_havok_version.md). The 2009 SDK is the ONLY one that works with the dead engine, anything newer breaks the constraint solver and you get goddamn jelly bodies that look like the studio went into the dirt all over again.

EAT IT.

inspector_skeleton.title: SKELETON. THE BONE HIERARCHY
inspector_skeleton.body:
Read-only view of the loaded character's bone hierarchy. Bone names, parent indices, bind-pose transforms.

USE: when you need to know what bone is where, what bone is the parent of what, what bone owns the bow position. The 'Bone_LHand' name comes from here, no fucking guessing.

Not editable from this panel. The skeleton is baked into the .mdl asset.

EAT IT.

inspector_bones.title: BONES TAB. PER-BONE WORLD TRANSFORM TABLE
inspector_bones.body:
Same as Skeleton but in tabular form: every bone, its current world matrix, its parent, its child count. Click a bone to highlight it in the viewport overlay.

USE: debugging why a weapon is at the wrong fucking bone, verifying which bone has the verts you're trying to manipulate. The 'wait why is the bow at the shoulder' inspector.

EAT IT.

lua_dependencies.title: LUA DEPENDENCIES. WHICH .LUA FILES INCLUDE WHICH
lua_dependencies.body:
The fucking spider-web of include chains Pandemic shipped before the studio went into the dirt. cutscene_helmsdeep.lua includes character_anims.lua includes combat_anims.lua includes some bastard helper that nobody remembers writing. This tab reconstructs the dependency graph so you don't have to grep through a hundred goddamn files to find where the fuck a behavior gets defined.

USE: figuring out which file to edit when you want to change behavior X. Search for X in this tab, see which file owns it, click to open. Saves an entire afternoon of cursing at the dump dir.

EAT IT.

lua_browser.title: LUA BROWSER. FILE TREE OF EVERY .LUA IN THE LEVEL
lua_browser.body:
Flat tree of every cursed .lua file the level references. Click to open in the tabbed editor. Reconstructed from the dump dir because Pandemic's source-side asset browser died with the studio and we had to build a new one out of byte salad.

USE: navigation. Cleaner than grepping 'find file by name' when you know roughly where it lives in the source tree but can't remember the exact goddamn filename. The 'where the fuck did I put that script' panel.

EAT IT.

lua_diff.title: LUA DIFF. WHAT'S CHANGED VS THE ORIGINAL PAK
lua_diff.body:
Side-by-side diff: original Lua content (from the PAK as Pandemic shipped before the EA buzzsaw) vs your edited version. Highlights line-level changes in eye-stabbing color so you can see exactly what got fucked with.

USE: pre-flight check before Save Level. Verify you haven't accidentally introduced trailing whitespace or some other invisible mistake that breaks the parser. The Lua runtime in this engine swallows parse errors silently and pretends nothing happened, which is one of the joys Pandemic left us before the layoffs hit. Saves you from shipping a bug that takes a goddamn hour to track down because the engine won't tell you a single fucking thing about why your script does nothing.

EAT IT.

lua_models.title: LUA MODELS REFERENCED. WHICH MODELS DOES THE LUA TOUCH
lua_models.body:
Static analysis pass over the loaded Lua: which model assets get referenced by name in the cursed scripts. The 'don't fucking miss one' panel.

USE: when you're renaming a model and need to update every script that uses it without missing one. Miss a single reference and you ship a dangling CRC that the engine silently chokes on, dump dir gets noisy, in-game nothing happens, and you spend an afternoon hunting the bastard down through the byte salad.

EAT IT.

timeline_blending.title: BLENDING SECTION. CROSS-FADE CONFIG BETWEEN STATES
timeline_blending.body:
The motherfucking heart of why Pandemic's anim transitions don't look like a brainrotted slideshow. Per-state-transition blend duration. State A's playback fades out over D seconds while state B fades in. The cross-fade between two clips, the unsung hero of every action game ever shipped.

FIELDS: blend in (seconds), blend out (seconds), blend curve (linear/ease-in/ease-out/custom).

DANGER: zero blend = pop, looks like horseshit, like the character had a goddamn seizure mid-attack. >1 second blend = visible drift on locomotion, looks like the character is ice-skating around like a brainrotted muppet. Pandemic typical is 0.15-0.3s and that's the fucking sweet spot, anything outside that range and you've broken something they spent years tuning.

EAT IT.

timeline_events.title: EVENTS SECTION. FIRE TRIGGERS AT SPECIFIC FRAMES
timeline_events.body:
Per-clip event flags. At frame F, fire event E. Used for footstep audio, hitbox-on/off, particle spawn, dialog cue. The thing that makes attacks land WHEN they look like they should and not a goddamn quarter-second late.

HOW TO USE:

1. Click ADD EVENT.
2. Pick the frame, the event name, the parameters.
3. SAVE writes to the clip's event list.

SHIT TO WATCH:

- Events fire ONCE per playback. If the runtime restarts the clip (loop), they fire again. Most Pandemic clips have a handful of events; over ~20 per clip is unusual and probably wrong.

EAT IT.

timeline_bones.title: BONES ROWS. PER-BONE CHANNEL VIEW
timeline_bones.body:
Each visible bone gets a horizontal row showing where keys exist on its channels. Click a key dot to select it. Drag to move in time.

FILTER bar at the top narrows visible bones. 'hand', 'spine', 'foot_l' etc. With 60+ bones per character a filter is fucking essential or you're scrolling forever.

EAT IT.

timeline_pose.title: POSE SNAPSHOT. COPY/PASTE A BONE POSE ACROSS TIME
timeline_pose.body:
Capture every visible bone's current transform to a clipboard. Paste at a different time to copy the pose to that frame. The 'I need this exact fucking pose at frame 47 too' button.

USE: matching the start and end of a loop, copying an anchor pose between clips, building hold frames.

DANGER: paste OVERWRITES keys at the target time. Verify the time before pasting or you'll nuke a goddamn key you needed.

EAT IT.

browser_models.title: MODELS TAB. EVERY MESH IN THE PAK
browser_models.body:
Filterable list of every model in the loaded PAK. Heroes (CH_), crowds (CRD_), weapons (WP_), props (PR_), level geo, foliage. The whole goddamn library.

Double-click to open in Model Viewer. Right-click for Export / Duplicate / Find References.

EAT IT.

browser_animations.title: ANIMATIONS TAB. EVERY CLIP IN THE PAK
browser_animations.body:
Filterable list of every animation clip. Click to see frame count, sample rate, target skeleton.

Double-click to play on the current preview rig. Right-click for Export / Duplicate / Find References.

DANGER: playing an anim on the wrong skeleton (mismatched bone count) silently does fuck-all or produces glitches. Match anim and rig.

EAT IT.

browser_materials.title: MATERIALS TAB. EVERY MAT1/MAT2/MAT3/MAT4 ENTRY
browser_materials.body:
Filterable list of every material in Block1. Per-material: tex0/tex1/tex2/tex3 refs, shader register state, blend mode.

Click to open in Asset Data Inspector for field-level edit.

SHIT YOU NEED TO KNOW: this is where the crowd shader probes happened. Mat edits CAN change rendered output for non-crowd meshes, but the crowd subsystem hardcodes to tex0 ignoring material data (see project_crowd_shader_limits.md). So editing tex2 on a crowd does fucking nothing in-game.

EAT IT.

browser_effects.title: EFFECTS TAB. PARTICLES, DECALS, SCREEN-SPACE FX
browser_effects.body:
Filterable list of every FX entry. Per-FX: emitter type, lifetime, particle count, shader bundle ref.

FX_*.bin files are the shader bundles for these effects. Edits to FX data require repacking the FX bundle, which is a fucking adventure on its own.

EAT IT.

eg_overview.title: EVENT GRAPH OVERVIEW. LAYER-TREE VIEW OF EVERY EVENT NODE
eg_overview.body:
Top-level navigation view. Entities organized by their layer (templateLevel > Layers > Entities), with event edges drawn between them.

CLICK a layer to expand. CLICK an entity to see its edges. Use this for getting your fucking bearings on a level you haven't worked in before.

EAT IT.

eg_explorer.title: EVENT GRAPH EXPLORER. SEARCHABLE LIST + TREE
eg_explorer.body:
Search bar + filterable tree. Find an entity by name, see its full event chain (incoming + outgoing).

USE: 'I know there's a trigger_volume that fires the cutscene, where the hell is it'. Type 'cutscene', see every entity that touches a cutscene event.

EAT IT.

eg_matrix.title: EVENT GRAPH MATRIX. WHO-FIRES-WHAT GRID
eg_matrix.body:
NxN grid: rows = source entities, columns = target entities. Cell shows the event name if a wire exists. Useful for spotting fan-outs (one trigger to many targets) and fan-ins (many triggers to one target). The 'why the fuck does this one trigger do TEN things' view.

EAT IT.

eg_modes.title: EVENT GRAPH MODES. GAMEMODE-SPECIFIC EDGE OVERLAY
eg_modes.body:
Levels can have multiple gamemodes (Conquest vs Team Deathmatch). Each mode activates a different layer subset, which means a different event subgraph. This tab shows the per-mode active subgraph.

USE: 'why does this trigger work in CQ but not TDM'. Check this tab, see which mode the trigger's layer belongs to. Saves a fuckload of in-game testing.

EAT IT.

eg_properties.title: EVENT GRAPH PROPERTIES. PER-EDGE FIELD EDITOR
eg_properties.body:
Select an edge in the graph, this tab shows its fields: source event, target input, condition, delay, repeat count.

Edit in place. Save Level commits.

DANGER: editing the event name to one the target entity doesn't accept (case-sensitive!) breaks the wire silently in-game. logic_relay takes 'Trigger', not 'Activate'. Wire it wrong and nothing fucking happens, no error, no warning.

EAT IT.

create_entity.title: CREATE ENTITY WIZARD. SPAWN A NEW GAMEOBJ
create_entity.body:
Pandemic's entity spawn dialog. Pick a type, the wizard pre-fills required fields based on that type's schema, drops the entity at the current camera target. Beats the fuck out of editing the binary by hand.

HOW TO USE:

1. TYPE picker: spawn_point_team_A, light_sun, capture_zone, etc.
2. NAME: must be unique within the level.
3. LAYER: which layer the new entity gets parented to. Defaults to the currently-active layer.
4. POSITION: editable, defaults to camera target.
5. REQUIRED FIELDS: type-specific (capture_zone needs an owner team, etc.). The wizard validates.
6. CREATE button: spawns. Save Level commits.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Spawning with an existing name CRC creates a collision. The wizard checks but typos can slip through and you'll get a goddamn dupe.
- Some types need a hierarchy hookup that the wizard can't infer. Check the spawned entity's Inspector for missing CRC refs after spawn.

EAT IT.

create_kit.title: CREATE CONSTRUCTION KIT. SPAWN A LEVEL-BLOCK GROUP
create_kit.body:
Pandemic's level designers worked with 'construction kits': pre-grouped sets of entities (a complete capture zone with its trigger, its flag, its spawn points, its UI markers) that you stamp as one fucking unit instead of placing them all individually.

HOW TO USE:

1. KIT picker: which kit type to spawn.
2. POSITION: where the kit's pivot lands.
3. PARAMS: per-kit (team owner, capture time, etc.).
4. CREATE: spawns ALL the kit's child entities at once.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Kit save pipeline has known CRC mismatch bugs in some configurations (see project_kit_save_bugs.md). Test the spawned kit in-game before committing major work or you'll be reverting.
- Kits with hardcoded GUIDs collide if you spawn the same kit twice. Pandemic's kits are designed for 1-per-level use typically.

EAT IT.

create_gamemode.title: CREATE GAMEMODE. ADD A NEW GAMEMODE TO THE LEVEL
create_gamemode.body:
Multi-gamemode levels (Conquest, Team Deathmatch, Hero, Ring Bearer) each activate a different layer subset. This wizard adds a new gamemode entry to the level's GameModeMask data.

HOW TO USE:

1. GAMEMODE NAME: must match a runtime-recognized string.
2. LAYERS active in this mode: checkbox list.
3. SPAWN OVERRIDES: which spawn points this mode uses (different teams have different spawns per mode).
4. WIN CONDITION: how the mode ends (capture %, time, kill count).

DANGER: the runtime engine ships with a fixed gamemode name table. Adding a custom name silently falls back to the default mode in-game unless you also patch the EXE. So if you 'add' a mode and nothing fucking happens, that's why.

EAT IT.

crowd_mesh_builder.title: WELCOME TO THE FUCKING MEAT GRINDER
crowd_mesh_builder.body:
Bake a hero rig and a weapon together into a crowd archetype. Heroes get their weapons attached at runtime. Crowds get them WELDED into mesh slot[0] because EA shot Pandemic in the head before the runtime crowd-weapon-attach code shipped. The gap in the engine is filled here, at build time, with the file you are looking at.

HOW TO USE:

1. BASE MESH dropdown. Pick a hero (CH_) or an existing crowd (CRD_). The one with the bones you want.
2. WEAPON MESH dropdown. WP_*, PR_*. The thing you want welded.
3. ATTACH BONE dropdown. Bone_LHand for archery, Bone_RHand for swords. The bone the weapon's verts get rigid-weighted to.
4. OFFSET XYZ and ROTATION YPR. To position the weapon. The LIVE PREVIEW checkbox spawns the bow on top of the elf in the main viewport while you drag.
5. NEW MESH NAME. What to call the merged archetype. Has to be unique or lotrc_rs explodes at repack time. Pick INTENTIONALLY the same name only when you mean to overwrite a previous bake (e.g. iterating bow position).
6. BAKE button. Queues the merge. Does NOT fire immediately. The Python embed pipeline runs at Save Level time and writes the new model JSON. Then lotrc_rs -c repacks.

DANGERS that will fuck you:

- If your name collides with an existing one, lotrc_rs panics. Change it.
- If you pick an existing baked CRD as Base, you get TWO weapons welded on. Pick the stripped or source CRD, not the merged one.
- The atlas bake crops a region from the weapon's atlas and stuffs it into a corner of the base atlas. If your base atlas has no spare UV real estate, the bow renders pixelated. Solve by Mesh Surgery plus UV box first to free up atlas space.

EAT IT.

move_triangles.title: MOVE WELDED VERTS WITHOUT BURNING ANOTHER FIVE-MINUTE BAKE
move_triangles.body:
The bow is already in the elf's mesh. The old way to nudge it 3cm was: strip the bow, re-bake from stripped, repack with lotrc_rs, reload Vespucci. Five minutes per attempt. Each iteration burned a chunk of your fucking afternoon. This panel skips all of that.

HOW TO USE:

1. MODEL DROPDOWN (top of this section). Type into the FILTER box to find your model fast. 'bowtest', 'elf_ancn', 'orc_swd' all work. The full unfiltered list has hundreds of entries, the filter saves your scroll wheel.
2. EMBEDDED VIEWER. The bright preview rig lights the model so you can actually SEE it (bypasses Helm's Deep's atmospheric tonemap which would otherwise crush it dark).
3. RIGHT-DRAG inside the viewer to orbit. WHEEL to zoom.
4. LEFT-CLICK on a triangle to select it. SHIFT+CLICK adds another triangle to the selection.
5. GROW CONNECTED button. Floods the selection through shared vertices. Click a bow triangle, hit Grow a couple of times, the whole bow is selected.
6. DELTA XYZ slider. WORLD-SPACE translation. Drag and the selected verts move LIVE in the main viewport too.
7. APPLY button. Persists the delta to a sidecar JSON.
8. Save Level. Commits the delta to the model JSON. The Python pipeline reads the sidecar, applies translation to exactly the picked verts, then lotrc_rs -c repacks the PAK.

DANGERS:

- Apply only persists the CURRENT delta. Click Apply BEFORE moving on to a different model or your move is lost.
- Each Apply OVERWRITES the previous sidecar. Apply for one model, Save Level, then Apply for the next.
- The viewer is a bind-pose render. Animation does not run. Your move IS correct at bind pose, the engine's skinning applies the bone palette at runtime.

RIDE OR FUCKING DIE, KING.

adjust_baked_weapon.title: PICK A BONE, MOVE EVERY VERT WEIGHTED TO IT
adjust_baked_weapon.body:
Works on EVERY skinned CRD in the level. The ones YOU baked AND the shipped ones Pandemic welded together in 2009 before EA fed the goddamn studio to the woodchipper. Picks verts by skinning weight, not by mouse click. Best for when the bow or sword is already in a known bone-rigid configuration and you just want to grab everything in that fucking bone's territory.

HOW TO USE:

1. SKINNED MODEL dropdown. Every loaded CRD/CH with bones. If your model is not there, double-click it in the Level Loader first so the model cache picks it up.
2. BONE dropdown. Bone_LHand for archery, Bone_RHand for swords, etc. The status line tells you HOW MANY VERTS got selected, so you instantly know if you picked a useless animation-only bone (Bone_Root, Bone_GlobalSRT, those own zero verts).
3. DELTA XYZ sliders. BONE-LOCAL translation. Y is the bone's own up-axis, NOT world up. This is the right fucking space for moving a weapon because if the elf raises their arm, the move follows.
4. DELTA YPR sliders. Bone-local rotation. Yaw around bone Y, pitch around bone X, roll around bone Z.
5. APPLY. Persists the (model, bone, delta) tuple to a sidecar JSON.
6. Save Level. Python finds every vert weighted to that bone, applies bind_world * delta * inv(bind_world) to its position in the model JSON. Then lotrc_rs -c repacks.

DANGERS:

- 'No verts matched' means the bone IS in the skeleton but owns no verts in slot[0]. Pick a different bone or switch to Move Triangles for click-pick.
- Bone-LOCAL space means dragging Y=1 on Bone_LHand moves the bow along the FOREARM up-axis at bind pose, not world up. If the bone's bind orientation is tilted you see weird directions. Move Triangles is world-space if you want simple drag.
- Apply OVERWRITES the previous sidecar entry. One Apply, one Save Level, repeat. Forget that order and your previous edit gets fucking obliterated.

EAT IT.

mesh_surgery.title: STRIP A WELDED WEAPON OUT OF A SHIPPED CRD
mesh_surgery.body:
Pandemic baked weapons into CRD body meshes back in Maya before they got fucking slaughtered, so every shipped CRD has its sword/bow/banner sewn into slot[0] verts. This panel rips them out. UV-box mode is the surgical tool, bone-weight is the chainsaw, auto-find is the lazy bastard option.

HOW TO USE:

1. SOURCE MODEL. Pick the CRD with the welded weapon. Type into the filter to narrow.
2. ATLAS PREVIEW shows up next to the controls. The diffuse atlas of the model. The weapon's UV region is usually the corner or strip the user shipped it in.
3. THREE selection modes:
   - DRAW UV BOX: click and drag on the atlas to draw a rectangle. Every vert whose TextureCoord(0) falls inside the box gets queued for deletion.
   - AUTO-FIND: heuristic. Looks for verts at hand height that extend past the body Z bounds. Works on most rigs because weapons stick OUT, body parts stay IN. Click the button to see what it found highlighted green on the atlas.
   - BONE FILTER (older mode): every vert weighted to a stripped bone gets deleted. UV-box and bone can combine.
4. NEW NAME. The stripped output is written as a NEW model JSON. The shipped CRD stays untouched.
5. STRIP & QUEUE. Queues the spec for the next Save Level cycle. The Python apply_strip_specs runs at save and produces models/<new_name>.json.

DANGERS:

- If your UV box overlaps body parts (hands, face), you delete them too. Visible holes in the elf where the goddamn hand used to be. Tighten the box.
- Auto-find sometimes catches arm cuffs because they ALSO stick out past body Z. Verify the green preview rectangle before stripping or you'll fuck up the silhouette.
- Stripping changes vert COUNTS which means triangle indices shift. Anything downstream that hardcoded vert indices (old bake sidecars) will be wrong.

EAT IT.

save_level.title: WHAT THE FUCK ACTUALLY HAPPENS WHEN YOU HIT SAVE LEVEL
save_level.body:
Save Level is the COMMIT button for the whole session. Every Apply, every bake, every strip, every property edit you made gets bundled and shipped to the Python pipeline. The pipeline runs level_patcher.py, which:

1. UNPACKS the original PAK to a temp dir using lotrc_rs -d.
2. PATCHES level.json with new entities, deleted GUIDs, field edits, the crowd block overlay.
3. APPLIES strip specs (Mesh Surgery's queued strips).
4. APPLIES merged-model specs (Crowd Mesh Builder's queued bakes).
5. APPLIES embedded weapon xforms (Move Triangles / Adjust Baked Weapon deltas).
6. REPACKS the temp dir back to a PAK using lotrc_rs -c.
7. REPLACES the original PAK + BIN with the new ones.

This takes minutes. A terminal window pops up with progress. DO NOT CLOSE IT. If the Python step errors out (lotrc_rs panic, name collision, bad spec), you LOSE all the unsaved edits from this session.

HOW TO USE:

1. Do your work. Bake meshes, move triangles, place crowds, whatever.
2. Hit Save Level (FILE menu, top of the program).
3. Wait for the terminal window. Watch the log for errors. Common ones:
   - 'name collision': your bake name conflicts. Change it.
   - 'verts list empty after bounds-check': the xforms sidecar references verts past the end of the model. Probably re-applied after the model JSON changed.
   - 'subprocess failed': lotrc_rs crashed. Usually a malformed JSON. The terminal shows which file.
4. Reload the level afterward to see the result.

DANGERS:

- Save fails halfway = partial commit. Some sidecars get consumed, others don't. Bug-prone state. If save errors, REVERT manually from the .bak files in the dump dir before re-saving.
- Save Level invokes Python subprocess. Slow on first save of a fresh dir because lotrc_rs has to unpack a 100MB PAK.
- The output PAK overwrites the input. Always have a backup of your original Levels/ dir before heavy editing.

EAT IT.

model_viewer.title: MODEL VIEWER. ONE MESH, BIND POSE, LIT BRIGHT AS GOD'S OWN MIDDLE FINGER
model_viewer.body:
Double-click an entity in the Level Loader / Asset Tree to open. Shows that one model in bind pose, lit by a neutral Maya-style rig (key + fill + ambient) so you can actually fucking see it independent of whatever atmospheric tonemap the level ships with. Black Gates won't make your mesh look like a black hole anymore. Bypasses Pandemic's Reinhard tonemap pipeline, which was calibrated for the cursed levels they shipped before the studio went into the dirt.

HOW TO USE:

1. ORBIT CAMERA. Right-drag to orbit. Wheel to zoom. Same controls as Move Triangles.
2. WIREFRAME toggle. Show triangle edges over the surface.
3. SHOW COLLISION toggle. If the model has a collision hull (BVTree or HkShape) it renders as a green wireframe overlay on top of the mesh. Lets you see what the physics engine sees vs what gets rendered.
4. Build Collision button. For models that DON'T have collision shapes shipped, this generates a triangle-mesh collision from the visual geometry. Used by the Havok bake pipeline.
5. Save Collision. Writes the generated shape to the model JSON.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- The viewer renders ONE model. No skinning, no animation, no context. Useful for material inspection, not for animation testing.
- The Save Collision button modifies the model JSON in place. Backup first if you're not sure or you'll be regenerating the goddamn collision from scratch.

EAT IT.

crowd_inspector.title: CROWD INSPECTOR. EVERY SINGLE FUCKER IN THE LEVEL, INDEXED AND SEARCHABLE
crowd_inspector.body:
Lists every 3dCrowd item (archetype) in the level, expandable to show every instance of that archetype, where they are, what animation they're running, what LOD radius, etc. Mirror of Pandemic's internal crowd browser, reconstructed from the binary 3dCrowd block by reading hex until the structure made fucking sense.

HOW TO USE:

1. ITEM tree. Top-level entries are archetypes (CRD_*). Click to expand and see every spawned instance.
2. Click an instance to FOCUS the main viewport on it. Camera flies over.
3. Per-instance fields:
   - Position XYZ. Editable. Drag the gizmo in the main viewport OR type values.
   - Rotation. Yaw only on crowds; pitch/roll usually 0.
   - LOD distance. How far the camera can be before the instance culls. Default 10000 (basically infinite).
4. Right-click an instance for the context menu: Delete, Clone, Set as Spawn Default.
5. ADD INSTANCE button. Spawns a new instance of the selected archetype at the camera target.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Deleting an instance is immediate. Save Level commits it. The .bak from the previous save is your only undo.
- Crowds inside disabled GameModeMask layers will render in this list but NOT in-game. Check the layer or you'll be staring at a guy who doesn't exist when the player loads in.

EAT IT.

crowd_generator.title: CROWD GENERATOR. STAMP A WALL OF FUCKERS IN ONE CLICK
crowd_generator.body:
Stamp N copies of a crowd archetype inside a radius. For setting up battle scenes without manually placing each elf, orc, or hobbit one at a fucking time.

HOW TO USE:

1. ARCHETYPE dropdown. Which CRD to spawn.
2. COUNT. How many. 50-200 typical for a wall section. Stops cooperating past ~5000 because the 3dCrowd block has its own internal limits.
3. CENTER XYZ. Where the disc center sits. Defaults to the camera target.
4. RADIUS. Disc radius in meters. Each instance gets a sqrt-uniform sample inside the disc so density is even across area.
5. JITTER Y. Vertical wobble in meters. Add +/- 0.1 to break the perfectly-flat-ground look that screams 'I was generated'.
6. RANDOM YAW checkbox. Each instance gets a random facing. Off = all face -Z (engine default).
7. SPAWN N HERE button. One-shot. Adds N instances. Save Level commits.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- 5000 instances stutters at LOD cull time. Game engine wasn't built for that count, Pandemic capped their armies smaller.
- Random yaw on archers makes the formation look weird in cinematic shots. Turn off for parade formations.
- The terrain underneath the disc must support the instances. If they spawn inside geometry, the engine renders them but they look stuck in walls and the player will see arms poking out of the goddamn ground.

EAT IT.

level_panel.title: LEVEL PANEL. THE ENTITY LIST FOR THE WHOLE FUCKING MAP
level_panel.body:
Every GameObj entity in the level. Spawn points, capture zones, light_sun, AtmosphereSetting, cinematic cameras, trigger volumes, AI waypoints, sound emitters. Anything Pandemic's level designers placed by hand using their internal editor (ZeroEdit) sits in this list.

HOW TO USE:

1. FILTER bar at the top. Type to narrow by name. 'spawn', 'light', 'cinematic', etc.
2. TYPE filter dropdown. Restrict to one type at a time (light_sun, AtmosphereSetting, spawn_point_team_A, etc.).
3. Click an entity to SELECT it. Highlighted in the main viewport. Inspector panel opens with its properties.
4. Double-click to FOCUS camera on it.
5. Right-click for context menu: Duplicate, Delete, Wipe (deletes with cascade cleanup).
6. CREATE button at the top. Wizard for spawning new entities by type, with hierarchy wiring (parent/child GUIDs, capture_zone owners, etc.). The wizard pre-fills common required fields per type.

DANGERS:

- DELETING an entity removes it from the level but does NOT clean up references. Other entities that pointed at it now have dangling CRC refs. Use WIPE instead, which scans and zeros the dangling refs.
- DUPLICATING copies the entire Block1 payload of the source entity. If the source had CRC/STRING/CRCLIST fields pointing at OTHER GUIDs in the source level, those references won't resolve in the copy. The duplicate-sanitizer zeroes them at save time, but verify your duplicated capture zones don't trigger 'who owns this' bugs in-game.

EAT IT.

event_graph.title: EVENT GRAPH. THE LEVEL'S TRIGGER WIRING, EXHUMED FROM A BINARY SHITSHOW
event_graph.body:
Pandemic's level scripting wasn't Lua, it was a visual event graph. Trigger volume fires > logic_relay activates > sound emitter starts plus AI patrol changes plus capture zone unlocks. This panel reconstructs that graph from the level's binary event chain data because the source-side editor went into the goddamn dumpster with the rest of Pandemic.

HOW TO USE:

1. NODES. Each entity that's part of the event chain shows as a node. Boxes connected by directed edges.
2. Click a node to inspect its inputs/outputs in the side panel.
3. EDGES are 'on event X, fire input Y on entity Z'. The graph visualizes these one-way.
4. FILTER by team (Good/Evil/Neutral) or by event type (Trigger, Activate, Kill, Damage, etc.).
5. SEARCH bar. Find a node by name. Search highlights all matching nodes and dims the rest.

DANGERS:

- The engine's event names are case-sensitive. logic_relay accepts 'Trigger' not 'Activate'. Wiring an Activate edge to a relay does fuck-all in-game.
- Deleting an entity in the Level panel does NOT remove its edges in the event graph. Save Level cleanup zeroes dangling refs but the topology can end up confused. Use Wipe.
- Some shipped levels have circular event chains that Pandemic's runtime tolerated but our graph layout chokes on. The graph view falls back to a flat list when it detects a cycle.

EAT IT.

inspector.title: INSPECTOR. EVERY GODDAMN FIELD ON THE SELECTED ENTITY, EDITABLE IN PLACE
inspector.body:
Every field of the selected GameObj entity, with type info and live edit. Saves changes through the FieldEdit pipeline so they persist past Save Level. Mirror of Pandemic's per-entity property sheet, reconstructed from the binary schema after EA pulled the plug while the code was still bleeding. The motherfucking heart of entity authoring, dragged out of the byte salad one offset at a time.

HOW TO USE:

1. Select an entity in the Level panel or click it in the main viewport. The inspector populates.
2. Each field shows: NAME, TYPE (int/float/string/CRC/GUID/Vec3/WorldTransform/etc.), CURRENT VALUE, edit widget.
3. Edit the value. The widget validates by type (int field rejects letters, GUID field rejects non-hex).
4. Edits queue into the FieldEdit list. Save Level commits them to the level's Block1.
5. RESET button reverts the current entity's pending edits.
6. APPLY button forces a queue commit without saving the level (useful for testing changes against the runtime preview).

DANGERS:

- WorldTransform fields control where the entity sits in space. Edit Position via the gizmo in the main viewport, not by typing matrix values, unless you actually want to fight quaternions by hand like a goddamn masochist.
- Some fields are CRC references to OTHER entities. Edit the value to an unresolvable CRC and the engine silently ignores the reference at load time. Use the dropdown picker that the inspector offers for CRC-typed fields when it has the level loaded.
- Float fields don't get auto-rounded. Type 0.300000001 and that's what gets written.

EAT IT.

anim_graph.title: ANIMATION GRAPH. THE STATE MACHINE WIRING FOR ONE CHARACTER, RIPPED FROM THE GODDAMN BINARY
anim_graph.body:
Pandemic's character animation runs through a per-character state machine: idle > draw_weapon > attack > hit_reaction > etc. The state machine is data, lives in a Lua-generated graph that the runtime reads. This panel reconstructs and lets you edit it directly instead of fighting the Lua source pipeline that no longer fucking exists.

HOW TO USE:

1. CHARACTER picker. Which character/CRD's anim graph to view.
2. NODES are states. Each has an associated clip name (the actual animation asset CRC).
3. EDGES are transitions. Each carries a condition (event, timer, blend, immediate).
4. Click a node to inspect: clip name, loop mode, playback rate, blend in/out time.
5. Click an edge to inspect: trigger condition, blend duration.
6. Add/Delete nodes via right-click. Add edges by drag-drop between nodes.

DANGERS:

- Clips referenced by name MUST exist in the animation asset bank for the character. If you reference a missing clip, the state silently falls back to idle, hiding the bug.
- Some shipped graphs have unreachable states (no incoming edges). The runtime tolerates it but the graph layout shows them floating. Not a bug, just dead data Pandemic left in.
- Editing the graph does NOT regenerate the underlying Lua. Save Level commits the binary form directly. Lua side stays stale (and we don't really need it because the binary is what the engine reads).

EAT IT.

lua_editor.title: LUA EDITOR. CRACK OPEN PANDEMIC'S SCRIPT CORPSE AND TYPE OVER IT
lua_editor.body:
Pandemic used Lua for some level-time scripting (intro cutscenes, scripted AI sequences, dialog triggers). This editor opens those scripts inline with syntax highlighting and incremental compile so you don't have to fucking grep through the dump dir to find a script.

HOW TO USE:

1. FILE TREE on the left. Every .lua referenced by the level. Click to open in the tabbed view.
2. TABBED EDITOR. Standard text editor. Tabs persist across sessions.
3. SAVE button per tab. Writes the .lua back to the dump dir.
4. SYNTAX CHECK button. Runs a parser pass and shows errors inline. Doesn't catch runtime errors, only parse-level mistakes.
5. The Lua isn't strictly required for the level to work. It's an interpretation layer Pandemic used for cutscene timing.

DANGERS:

- The runtime Lua interpreter is the one shipped with the engine. It's not standard Lua 5.1, it has Pandemic extensions and missing stdlib pieces. Test edits in-game before assuming they work.
- Lua errors at runtime are SILENT in shipped builds. Use the editor's syntax check before save or you'll ship a script that does fuck-all and never tells you why.
- Save Level packs the .lua bytes back into the PAK. If you broke the parse, the level still loads but the script does nothing.

EAT IT.

crowd_mesh_builder_strip.title: STRIP BAKED WEAPON. THE SISTER SECTION TO MESH SURGERY
crowd_mesh_builder_strip.body:
Embedded inside Crowd Mesh Builder because sometimes you want to strip AND re-bake in one save cycle. Same engine as Mesh Surgery, same UV-box / auto-find / bone-filter modes, same Python apply at save time. Saves a fucking trip to the standalone Mesh Surgery panel.

WHY IT'S DUPLICATED HERE:

Mesh Surgery is the standalone panel for ripping weapons out and being done. This sub-section is for when you're inside the Crowd Mesh Builder workflow and realize the base mesh you picked still has Pandemic's shipped weapon welded on. You strip it from here without leaving the bake panel, then proceed straight into BAKE.

HOW TO USE: same as Mesh Surgery (see that card). Pick mode, define the verts to delete, name the output, queue the strip. Save Level applies.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- The stripped output is a NEW model JSON. Make sure your bake step references the STRIPPED name, not the shipped name, or you'll bake a weapon onto a CRD that still has its old weapon and end up with two goddamn bows.
- Don't strip + bake to the SAME name. lotrc_rs panics on collisions.

EAT IT.

cinematic_spline.title: 3D SPLINE EDIT MODE (FABRIK). YANK CAMERA HANDLES IN THE VIEWPORT
cinematic_spline.body:
Toggle this and the SplineEditor draws handles + extend arrows directly in the 3D viewport. Drag the handles to reshape the cinematic camera's path. FABRIK keeps the spline smooth while you drag a single control point so you don't have to manually re-tween adjacent points by hand like a fucking caveman.

WHAT FABRIK MEANS HERE:

Forward And Backward Reaching Inverse Kinematics. Same algorithm used for character limb IK, repurposed for spline-handle dragging. You yank one handle and the surrounding handles slide along the path to keep curvature consistent. Without FABRIK you'd get sharp kinks every time you moved a point and the cutscene camera would jerk like it's having a goddamn stroke.

HOW TO USE:

1. Pick a cinematic_camera entity (top of the panel).
2. Click ENTER 3D SPLINE EDIT MODE. The viewport sprouts colored spheres at every spline control point plus arrows at the ends for extending the path.
3. LEFT-CLICK and DRAG a sphere to move that control point. FABRIK smooths the surrounding points.
4. CLICK an arrow at either end to extend the path by one new handle.
5. RIGHT-CLICK a sphere to delete that handle.
6. Click EXIT 3D SPLINE EDIT MODE to turn off the handles and go back to normal viewport.

DANGERS:

- Edits are LIVE. They write to the camera's spline_data immediately. Save Level commits.
- The exit-mode toggle is important. Forgetting to exit means clicks in the viewport hit the spline handles instead of selecting entities and you'll be wondering why selection is fucking broken.

EAT IT.

bezier_rotation.title: ROTATION TAB. QUATERNION CURVE HANDLES
bezier_rotation.body:
The cursed bezier control for the rotation quaternion at the current keyframe. Drag the in/out tangent handles to reshape how the rotation eases into or out of this key. Looks like a normal curve editor, behaves like a goddamn unhinged math demon under the hood.

WARNING about quaternion space: the curve interpolates COMPONENT-WISE on the quaternion. A 'smooth' looking curve does NOT necessarily produce smooth visual rotation, because quaternion components aren't fucking independent and the math doesn't give a single shit about your eyeball estimate. For complex rotations, prefer ease-in/ease-out presets over hand-drawn bezier curves or you'll spend an entire afternoon wondering why your rotation looks like a brainrotted bastard having a seizure.

EAT IT.

bezier_translation.title: TRANSLATION TAB. PER-AXIS POSITION CURVE
bezier_translation.body:
The well-behaved cousin of the rotation tab, thank fuck. Bezier handles for the translation channel at the current keyframe. Drag tangents to control how the bone moves through this key. Translation is per-axis so X/Y/Z each have their own curve (switch via the axis picker).

Unlike the rotation channel, translation curves DO produce intuitive motion: smooth curve = smooth movement. No quaternion-space bullshit, no math demon waiting to fuck you over. What you draw is what you get, which is rare in this whole codebase so enjoy it while it lasts.

EAT IT.

bezier_scale.title: SCALE TAB. PER-AXIS SCALE CURVE
bezier_scale.body:
The third-class citizen of the bezier tabs. Most level entities ignore animated scale entirely (Pandemic never bothered wiring it on gameobjs, broken by design from the start), but characters use it for stretchy attack anims and impact deformation. Same per-axis convention as translation. Pull a scale curve hard and your hero's sword swing reads like it's made of pure hatred.
