DANGERS: extreme scale values (>2 or <0.5) can break skinning math and you'll get clipping, holes, inverted normals, the whole goddamn shitshow. Test in-game or your hero ends up looking like a balloon animal having a fucking stroke.

EAT IT.

inspector_environment.title: ENVIRONMENT TAB. SKYBOX + ATMOSPHERIC SETTINGS
inspector_environment.body:
Per-level environment config. Picks the skybox (the cubemap that fills the background), the cloud layer, the fog settings, the atmospheric tonemap parameters. This is what makes Helm's Deep look like Helm's Deep and Black Gates look like Black fucking Gates.

WHAT'S IN HERE:

- SKYBOX picker: which .hk cubemap to use. Choices come from the loaded GameFiles scan. Hit Rescan if your new skybox isn't in the list.
- CLOUD LAYER toggle: enable/disable the animated cloud overlay. Separate cubemap for clouds.
- FOG settings: color, density, start/end distance.
- ATMOSPHERE: tonemap curve (the Reinhard parameters the renderer uses to compress HDR into LDR), white point, exposure.
- TIME OF DAY: shifts the sun position. Drives the lighting direction.

HOW TO USE:

1. Pick a skybox from the dropdown. The viewport updates immediately.
2. Toggle clouds, pick a cloud cubemap. The renderer composites them over the skybox.
3. Adjust fog/tonemap/exposure to taste.
4. Save Level commits these to the AtmosphereSetting entity in Block1.

DANGERS:

- Extreme exposure values blow out the scene. The default Pandemic atmospheres are calibrated for the levels they ship with, fuck with them at your own risk.
- Picking a skybox that doesn't exist in the PAK leaves the background black at runtime. Skybox refs are by CRC, must match an actual asset.

EAT IT.

lua_treeview.title: TREE VIEW TAB. FOLDER HIERARCHY OF THE LUA SOURCE
lua_treeview.body:
Same files as the Browser tab but in folder-tree layout instead of flat list. For when you know which directory your script lives in (cutscenes/, ai/, gameplay/) and want to navigate by folder instead of guessing the goddamn filename.

Click a folder to expand. Click a file to open in the tabbed editor.

EAT IT.

lua_source.title: SOURCE TAB. THE ACTUAL CODE EDITOR
lua_source.body:
The text editor where you actually edit the Lua. Tabs along the top for currently-open files. Syntax highlighting for Lua keywords, strings, comments, numbers. Not a fucking IDE but it does the job.

HOW TO USE:

1. Open a file via Browser or Tree View. It appears as a tab here.
2. Edit the code. CTRL+S saves the tab to the dump dir.
3. CTRL+TAB cycles through open tabs.
4. The SYNTAX CHECK button at the bottom runs a parse pass and shows errors inline (red squiggles).

DANGERS:

- The editor saves to the DUMP DIR, not directly into the PAK. Save Level packs the changes into the PAK afterward.
- Lua runtime errors are SILENT in shipped game builds. Syntax check catches parse errors but not 'nil table index' style runtime crashes that will fuck you in-game with no warning.

EAT IT.

asm_graph_params.title: GRAPH PARAMETERS. NAMED VARIABLES THE STATE MACHINE READS
asm_graph_params.body:
Pandemic's state machines read named parameters at runtime to decide transitions. Speed > 0.5 means 'use locomotion clip'. IsAiming == true means 'use aim layer'. This section exposes every parameter the loaded graph reads.

EDIT live: change a parameter's current value and watch the graph state respond in the preview. Saves a fuckload of guess-and-check in-game.

DANGER: parameter names must match what the Lua runtime sets. Typos = silent fallback to default and you'll be wondering why your transition never fires.

EAT IT.

asm_creature_vars.title: CREATURE VARIABLES (CV_*). PER-CHARACTER STATE
asm_creature_vars.body:
CV_ prefix vars are Pandemic's per-instance character variables: CV_Health, CV_Stamina, CV_HasWeapon, etc. Animation graphs read these to decide transitions ('if CV_Health < 0.2, switch to limping locomotion'). The shit that makes characters behave differently when they're hurt.

VIEW: every CV the loaded graph references. Live value if the runtime is feeding them. Empty if the graph is loaded standalone.

DANGER: writing CVs from here only affects the preview. In-game, the Lua and game code set them, not this fucking panel.

EAT IT.

asm_lua_browser.title: LUA SCRIPT BROWSER. INLINE VIEW OF THE GRAPH'S LUA SOURCE
asm_lua_browser.body:
If the loaded graph has companion Lua scripts (animTable.lua, transitions.lua, etc.), they show up here for read-only inspection. For full editing use the standalone Lua Editor panel.

USE: cross-reference what the binary state machine does vs what the Lua source intended. Drift between them is fucking common after manual binary edits.

EAT IT.

asm_state_entries.title: ANIMATION STATE ENTRIES. RAW LIST OF EVERY STATE
asm_state_entries.body:
Flat list view of every state in the loaded graph. Name, clip reference, loop mode, blend params, transition count. Useful for spotting outliers (a state with zero transitions in or out is dead fucking weight, Pandemic left a lot of those in by accident before EA dropped the goddamn hammer).

CLICK a row to highlight that state in the graph view.

EAT IT.

asm_parity.title: ASM PARITY TOGGLES. WHICH CHECKS TO RUN ON LOAD
asm_parity.body:
Configures which parity checks the panel runs when comparing binary vs Lua:

- STATE COUNT check.
- TRANSITION COUNT check.
- CLIP NAME REFS check.
- BLEND TIME EQUALITY check.
- LOOP MODE check.

Turn off the noisy ones if a shipped graph has accepted drift you don't want flagged. Defaults are all on. Toggle them off when the false-positives are drowning out the shit you actually care about.

EAT IT.

add_event_popup.title: ADD EVENT POPUP. INSERT A TRIGGER FLAG AT CURRENT FRAME
add_event_popup.body:
Modal that opens when you click ADD EVENT in the Timeline Events section. Asks for the event name, parameters, and confirms the time (defaults to playhead position).

FIELDS:

- TIME (seconds): defaults to playhead. Editable for precise placement.
- EVENT NAME: dropdown of Pandemic's recognized event types (footstep_l, footstep_r, hitbox_on, hitbox_off, particle_spawn, dialog_cue, etc.) or custom string.
- PARAMETERS: depends on event type. Footstep takes a surface tag. Hitbox takes a damage value. Particle takes an FX ref.

ADD button writes the event into the clip. Save Level commits.

DANGER: custom event names that the runtime doesn't recognize fire SILENTLY in-game (the engine logs but the player sees fuck-all). Use the dropdown unless you know what you're doing.

EAT IT.

confirm_crowd_delete.title: CONFIRM CROWD DELETE. ARE YOU SURE
confirm_crowd_delete.body:
Pops up before deleting a crowd instance. Single yes/no. There's no fucking undo for crowd edits, so this exists to catch accidental Delete-key presses.

CLICK YES to commit, NO to cancel. The .bak files from the previous Save Level are your only recovery if you say yes by accident, so think before you click.

EAT IT.

level_inspector_identity.title: IDENTITY. GUID + TYPE + NAME OF THE SELECTED ENTITY
level_inspector_identity.body:
Read-only metadata: the entity's CRC GUID (unique identifier within the level), its type name (gameobj subclass), its user-facing name.

The GUID is what every other entity uses to reference this one. If you see GUID 0xDEADBEEF in some field elsewhere, this is the entity that field is pointing at. The fucking address book.

Not editable from here. Type and GUID are baked at creation time.

EAT IT.

level_inspector_position.title: POSITION. WORLD-SPACE XYZ
level_inspector_position.body:
Three editable float fields for the entity's world position. Units are meters in Pandemic's coord system (Y is up, +Z is forward for most spawns).

Drag the field for a slider-style edit, double-click to type a precise value. Save Level commits.

DANGER: extreme values (>10000 in any axis) put the entity outside the level's culling bounds. The runtime still loads it but it's fucking invisible, hiding inside the void.

EAT IT.

level_inspector_rotation.title: ROTATION & SCALE. ORIENTATION + OPTIONAL SCALE
level_inspector_rotation.body:
Rotation is shown as Euler angles (yaw/pitch/roll) by default. Click the Quat toggle to switch to quaternion components if you need precision past Euler's gimbal lock issues.

SCALE is per-axis. Most level entities ignore animated/static scale (gameobj WorldTransform stores translation + rotation only) but characters and props sometimes honor it.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Editing in quaternion space without normalizing breaks the rotation. Stick to Euler unless you're scripted and know the fucking math.
- Scale != 1 on a static prop with collision will MISMATCH the collision hull because the hull is unscaled. The renderer scales the mesh, Havok doesn't scale the shape, so the player walks through the visible mesh because the physics sees the original size.

EAT IT.

asset_inspector_hex.title: RAW HEX DUMP. BYTES SIDE-BY-SIDE WITH ASCII
asset_inspector_hex.body:
When the typed-field view above isn't enough, expand this collapsing section to see the raw 16-bytes-per-row hex view of the entire struct, with ASCII gutter on the right.

USE: spotting unexpected non-zero bytes in 'unk_*' fields. Finding string patterns inside CRC-indexed structs. Debugging when the typed view shows a value that looks wrong and you want to verify the underlying bytes haven't been fucked up by some other write path.

Not directly editable here, it's a viewer. To change bytes, edit through the typed fields above.

EAT IT.

menu_file.title: FILE MENU. OPEN / SAVE / CLOSE LEVEL
menu_file.body:
Top-bar FILE menu. Contains the load/save/close commands for the level cycle.

ITEMS:

- OPEN LEVEL: opens a file dialog for a PAK file. Cockpit boots up with that level loaded.
- RECENT LEVELS: last 8 levels you opened. Click to re-load.
- SAVE LEVEL: runs the full Python pipeline (see save_level tip).
- CLOSE LEVEL: unloads everything. Useful before switching to a different level to free memory.
- EXIT: closes Vespucci. Unsaved edits are fucking gone.

HOTKEYS: CTRL+O opens, CTRL+S saves. Same as every editor since the dawn of time.

EAT IT.

menu_view.title: VIEW MENU. TOGGLE PANEL VISIBILITY
menu_view.body:
Every cockpit panel has a checkbox in this menu. Click to show, click again to hide. State persists in imgui.ini across sessions so you don't have to re-set your fucking layout every time.

GROUPS:

- Level: Level / Outliner / Layers / Event Graph / Level Blocks / Level Inspector / Editor Object
- Animation: Animation Graph / Timeline / Bezier / Lua AnimTable / Animation State Machine / Filter Selection
- Assets: Browser / Asset Data Inspector / Model Viewer / Inspector
- Crowds: 3dCrowd Editor / Crowd Inspector / Crowd Generator
- System: Viewport / Overlay / Gizmo Tools / The Forge

The cockpit ships with a sensible default layout. Reset Layout (View > Reset Layout) wipes any drags you made and restores it when you've trashed the layout beyond recognition.

EAT IT.

menu_tools.title: TOOLS MENU. THE HEAVY-DUTY BAKE/STRIP/SURGERY OPERATIONS
menu_tools.body:
Anything that touches asset bytes lives here. The shit that can break a level if you fuck it up.

ITEMS:

- CROWD MESH BUILDER: bake hero + weapon into a crowd archetype. See crowd_mesh_builder card.
- MESH SURGERY: strip welded weapons out of a CRD. See mesh_surgery card.
- ADJUST BAKED WEAPON: per-bone delta on an already-baked CRD. See adjust_baked_weapon card.
- CINEMATIC SETUP: edit cutscene cameras. See cinematic_setup card.
- LUA EDITOR: edit Lua scripts. See lua_editor card.
- ASSET DATA INSPECTOR (F6): raw struct editor. See asset_data_inspector card.

Each opens a dedicated panel. They share the Save Level pipeline.

EAT IT.

menu_help.title: HELP MENU. HOW TO USE + RESET TIPS + ABOUT
menu_help.body:
Three things:

- HOW TO USE (also accessible via the red button top-right): the survival card. Lists every tip in the JSON via 'Open any tip card...' submenu.
- RESET ALL TIPS: clears every dismissal, so first-touch popups fire again next time you open each panel. Useful for returning users who forgot what panels do or for screenshots.
- ABOUT: build info. Vespucci version, Magellan engine identity, the EA/Pandemic acknowledgment (rest in fucking pieces, Pandemic).

EAT IT.

load_level_gate.title: STOP. LOAD A FUCKING LEVEL BEFORE GOING FURTHER
load_level_gate.body:
The next 25 panels are dead weight without a level loaded. Event Graph, Outliner, Inspector, Browser, Crowd Generator, all of them read from the loaded level's Block1. No level = empty fucking panels = nothing to teach.

DO THIS:

1. Click the 'Open Level...' button on this popup (or use File > Open Level from the menubar).
2. Pick a PAK file from your RE/Levels or RE/mods/Levels directory. Helm's Deep is a good first one because it has every system Pandemic shipped.
3. Wait for the cockpit to light up. The viewport will render the level's terrain + entities.
4. Click NEXT on this popup to continue the tour.

WHY THIS GATE EXISTS:

We used to let the tour walk past this and the user would see 25 popups in a row pointing at empty panels. That's how you waste an afternoon. Now we stop you here until a level is loaded.

NEXT is disabled until the runtime reports a level is loaded. The button lights up when you're good to go.

EAT IT.

menu_animation.title: VIEW > ANIMATION SUBMENU. ANIM PANEL TOGGLES
menu_animation.body:
Every panel related to animation work, grouped under one submenu so you don't have to scroll the flat View list. Includes Timeline, Bezier Curve Editor, Inspector (anim mode), Animation Graph, Filter Selection + Graph State + Motion Matching.

Click a name to toggle visibility. State persists in imgui.ini. Same fucking deal as the rest of the View menu.

EAT IT.

menu_scripting.title: VIEW > SCRIPTING SUBMENU. LUA + STATE MACHINE PANELS
menu_scripting.body:
Every panel that touches Pandemic's Lua source or the binary state machine: Lua AnimTable, Animation State Machine, Lua Editor.

Click a name to toggle. The Lua side is mostly read-only reference (the runtime reads the binary form), but the editor exists for when you actually do need to patch a cutscene script and don't want to dive into the fucking dump dir.

EAT IT.

menu_theme.title: THEME MENU. PICK YOUR POISON
menu_theme.body:
Apply a different ImGui style preset. Currently ships with 'VS Code Dark' as the only option, which is what you've been staring at. More themes can land here as the user asks for them.

DANGER: changing theme reloads colors live but doesn't change layout. If a panel looks broken after a theme switch it's a separate fucking bug, not the theme.

EAT IT.

menu_vespucci.title: TOOLS > VESPUCCI SUBMENU. SURFACES FROM THE VESPUCCI NAMESPACE
menu_vespucci.body:
Vespucci is the codename for the smart-wiring + suggested-wires subsystem (see project_smart_wiring_progress.md). This submenu opens its surfaces: the Suggested Wires sidebar, the brain overlay, the wizard, etc.

Most users won't touch this shit. It's for power-flow authoring where the tool suggests which event wires to draw based on entity proximity + type heuristics. Useful when you're wiring a brand new level from scratch and don't want to do every fucking edge by hand.

EAT IT.

ctx_place_crowd_here.title: PLACE CROWD CHARACTER HERE. RIGHT-CLICK SPAWN SHORTCUT
ctx_place_crowd_here.body:
Right-click anywhere in the viewport on the ground plane and this option appears. Picks a crowd archetype from a submenu and stamps ONE instance at the click point. Bypasses the Crowd Generator panel when you just need a single guy somewhere fast without setting up a whole goddamn disc.

USE: dressing a scene with hand-placed individuals (a banner-bearer at the wall edge, a captain on the rampart) instead of generating a wall of N.

Save Level commits.

EAT IT.

addevent_categories.title: ADD EVENT CATEGORIES. WHAT EACH SUB-MENU CONTAINS
addevent_categories.body:
The Add Event modal groups Pandemic's event types into categories. Each sub-menu lists the events in that category. Saves you scrolling through 80 event names looking for the right one.

CATEGORIES:

- DAMAGE: ApplyDamage / ApplyDamageToTarget / DamageOBBArea / etc. Fires hitbox damage at specific frames during attack anims.
- TRAIL/VFX: particle spawns, trail emitters, decal placements. Tied to weapon swings, footsteps, impacts.
- SOUND: SFX cues. Footstep_l / footstep_r / weapon_swing / etc. Surface-tagged so the audio engine picks the right material sample.
- CAMERA: camera shakes, FOV punches, slow-mo triggers for cinematic hits.
- STATE: setflag / clearflag / pushstate. Used by the state machine to gate transitions during anim playback.
- PROJECTILE: spawn projectile entity at the right frame of a throw/shoot anim. Bow arrows, thrown daggers, etc.
- THROW: more specific throw events (lock-on target, release frame).
- BOW: archery-specific (draw frame, release frame, arrow-attached frame).
- CONTROLLER: rumble pulses, controller force feedback.

Pick a category, pick an event within it, set params, click ADD. The event lands at the playhead's current time.

SHIT THAT WILL FUCK YOU:

- Custom event names that the runtime doesn't know fire silently. Always pick from the categorized list unless you've extended the fucking engine.
- Frame timing matters. Damage events at the wrong frame produce hits that don't sync with the visual and the player sees the attack land before the sword reaches them.

EAT IT.

hotkeys.title: HOTKEYS. EVERY KEYBOARD SHORTCUT IN THE COCKPIT
hotkeys.body:
Pandemic's ZeroEdit used XSI-style hotkeys. Vespucci honors them. Memorize these, save fucking afternoons.

VIEWPORT CAMERA:

- RIGHT-DRAG: look around (FPS style)
- W / A / S / D: move while RMB held
- Q / E: descend / ascend on world Y
- SHIFT: sprint
- CTRL: crawl
- F: focus camera on selected entity (camera flies to it)
- ALT + LEFT-DRAG: orbit around selected entity (XSI style)
- MIDDLE-DRAG: pan camera
- WHEEL: zoom (in fly mode) or dolly (in orbit mode)

GIZMOS:

- W: translate gizmo
- E: rotate gizmo
- R: scale gizmo (most level entities ignore scale)
- ESC: deselect, gizmo off
- CTRL while dragging gizmo: snap to increments (set in Gizmo Tools panel)

PANEL HOTKEYS:

- F4: toggle Level Inspector
- F5: toggle Editor Object
- F6: toggle Asset Data Inspector
- F11: toggle Viewport fullscreen
- TAB: toggle The Forge

FILE:

- CTRL+O: open level
- CTRL+S: save level
- CTRL+W: close level
- CTRL+Q: exit

EDIT:

- CTRL+Z: undo (limited support, only for some fields)
- CTRL+Y: redo
- CTRL+D: duplicate selected entity
- DEL: delete selected entity (asks for confirm on crowds)
- CTRL+SHIFT+W: WIPE selected entity (delete + cascade-clean dangling refs)

SELECTION:

- LEFT-CLICK in viewport: select entity
- SHIFT + LEFT-CLICK: add to selection
- CTRL + LEFT-CLICK: toggle from selection
- CTRL+A: select all visible entities

TIMELINE:

- SPACE: play / pause
- LEFT / RIGHT arrow: step back / forward one frame
- HOME / END: jump to start / end
- L: toggle loop

TRIANGLE PICKER (Crowd Mesh Builder Move Triangles section):

- LEFT-CLICK on triangle: select
- SHIFT + LEFT-CLICK: add to selection
- G: grow selection through connected verts (same as Grow Connected button)
- R: reset selection

MEMORIZE THE FUCKING HOTKEYS. EAT IT.
